title: Economically Useful Plants and Entrepreneurial Botany

questions.chapter: Economically Useful Plants and Entrepreneurial Botany
questions.solution:
Cardamom, **Elettaria cardamomum**, belongs to **Zingiberaceae**, the ginger family, along with ginger and turmeric.

Black pepper is Piperaceae; chilli is Solanaceae.

questions.chapter: Economically Useful Plants and Entrepreneurial Botany
questions.solution:
Groundnut, **Arachis hypogaea** (Fabaceae), is a native of **Brazil** in South America.

It was brought to India by the Portuguese, and India is now among the largest producers; its seeds give edible oil and the oil cake is used as cattle feed and manure.

questions.chapter: Economically Useful Plants and Entrepreneurial Botany
questions.q: The botanical name of rice is:
questions.solution:
Rice is **Oryza sativa** of the family Poaceae.

Triticum aestivum is wheat, Zea mays is maize and Eleusine coracana is finger millet (ragi).

questions.chapter: Economically Useful Plants and Entrepreneurial Botany
questions.q: Cotton fibre is obtained from the:
options: Epidermal hairs of the seed coat
questions.solution:
Cotton (Gossypium) fibres are long **epidermal hairs of the seed coat**: surface fibres.

Jute is a stem (bast) fibre, coir comes from the fruit wall (mesocarp) of coconut, and sisal from leaves.

questions.chapter: Economically Useful Plants and Entrepreneurial Botany
questions.q: The yellow colour of turmeric is due to:
questions.solution:
**Curcumin** in the rhizome of turmeric (Curcuma longa) gives the colour and much of its antiseptic, anti-inflammatory value.

Capsaicin makes chilli pungent, piperine black pepper, and azadirachtin is from neem.

questions.chapter: Economically Useful Plants and Entrepreneurial Botany
questions.q: Azadirachtin, used as a natural pesticide, is obtained from:
questions.solution:
**Azadirachtin** is the active principle of **neem** (Azadirachta indica), concentrated in the seed kernel.

It repels insects and disrupts their feeding and moulting, so neem oil and neem cake are used as bio-pesticides.

questions.chapter: Economically Useful Plants and Entrepreneurial Botany
questions.q: Tectona grandis is economically important as a source of:
questions.solution:
**Tectona grandis** is **teak**, one of the finest **timbers**: strong, durable and resistant to termites and decay because of its natural oils.

It is used for furniture, doors, ship building and construction.

questions.chapter: Economically Useful Plants and Entrepreneurial Botany
questions.q: The oyster mushroom commonly grown on paddy straw in Tamil Nadu belongs to the genus:
questions.solution:
The oyster mushroom is **Pleurotus** (e.g. Pleurotus sajor-caju), easily grown on chopped paddy straw in polythene bags: a low-cost enterprise.

Agaricus is the button mushroom, Volvariella the paddy straw mushroom, and Amanita is poisonous.

questions.chapter: Economically Useful Plants and Entrepreneurial Botany
questions.q: Caffeine is the alkaloid present in:
questions.solution:
**Caffeine** is the stimulating alkaloid of **coffee** (Coffea arabica) seeds and **tea** (Camellia sinensis) leaves.

In moderate amounts it stimulates the nervous system and reduces drowsiness.

questions.chapter: Economically Useful Plants and Entrepreneurial Botany
questions.q: What is the dried endosperm of coconut, from which coconut oil is extracted, called?
questions.solution:
It is **copra**. Coconut (Cocos nucifera) endosperm is dried in the sun or a kiln and pressed for oil.

The residue, coconut oil cake, is used as cattle feed.

questions.chapter: Economically Useful Plants and Entrepreneurial Botany
questions.q: Name the genus of the tree whose latex is the main source of natural rubber.
questions.solution:
**Hevea** (Hevea brasiliensis, Euphorbiaceae), the Pará rubber tree.

The bark is tapped to collect latex, which is coagulated with acid, rolled into sheets and dried.

questions.chapter: Economically Useful Plants and Entrepreneurial Botany
questions.q: Name the active principle of Phyllanthus amarus (keezhanelli), used for liver disorders.
questions.solution:
Its active principle is **phyllanthin** (with hypophyllanthin).

The whole plant is used in Siddha medicine for jaundice and other liver disorders.

questions.chapter: Economically Useful Plants and Entrepreneurial Botany
questions.q: Sandalwood oil is distilled from the heartwood of which species (scientific name)?
questions.solution:
**Santalum album**, Indian sandalwood. The fragrant oil is concentrated in the heartwood and roots.

It is used in perfumes, soaps, cosmetics and incense; the wood is used for carving.

questions.chapter: Economically Useful Plants and Entrepreneurial Botany
questions.q: To which plant family do rice, wheat, maize and the millets all belong?
questions.solution:
All cereals and millets belong to **Poaceae** (Gramineae), the grass family.

Their fruit is a **caryopsis**, in which the fruit wall is fused with the seed coat; the starchy endosperm is what feeds most of the world.

questions.chapter: Economically Useful Plants and Entrepreneurial Botany
questions.q: Give an account of active principle and medicinal values of any two plants you have studied.
questions.solution:
Model answer (any two):

**1. Neem — Azadirachta indica (Meliaceae).** Active principle: **azadirachtin** (also nimbin). Medicinal value: antiseptic, antibacterial and antifungal; leaves are used for skin diseases and chickenpox, twigs as a toothbrush for oral health, neem oil for skin infections; it is also a natural insecticide.

**2. Turmeric — Curcuma longa (Zingiberaceae).** Active principle: **curcumin**. Medicinal value: antiseptic and anti-inflammatory; applied to wounds and skin problems, taken for cough and cold, and used as a blood purifier.

**3. Keezhanelli — Phyllanthus amarus (Phyllanthaceae).** Active principle: **phyllanthin** and hypophyllanthin. Medicinal value: used for jaundice and liver disorders; also diuretic.

**4. Aloe — Aloe vera.** Active principle: **aloin**. Medicinal value: leaf gel heals burns and wounds, is used in skin care, and is a laxative.

(Two plants, each with active principle and at least two uses, earn full marks.)
